connections.label: The women at the tomb
connections.explanation: Matthew 28:1–8 and Mark 16:1–8 both tell of women coming to the tomb at dawn after the Sabbath, an angel's message that Jesus is risen and goes before them to Galilee, and the women leaving in fear. Matthew adds an earthquake, the angel rolling back the stone, and the women running with great joy to tell the disciples. Mark ends with them saying nothing to anyone.

ends.sectionTitle: The Resurrection and the Great Commission
ends.excerpt: Now after the Sabbath, as it began to dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb.
When the Sabbath was past, Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices, that they might come and anoint him.

order.note: Most modern scholars hold that Mark wrote first and Matthew used his Gospel, while Augustine held that Matthew wrote first and Mark followed him as an abridger, so which drew on which is disputed.

sources.author: Raymond E. Brown
sources.title: An Introduction to the New Testament

connections.label: The household: wives, children, servants
connections.explanation: Ephesians 5:22–6:9 retells Colossians 3:18–4:1: wives and husbands, children and parents, servants and masters in that order, servants working as for the Lord and masters under a Master in heaven. Ephesians enlarges the word to husbands into Christ's love for the church, and quotes the commandment to honour father and mother.

ends.sectionTitle: The New Life; the Household; Greetings
ends.excerpt: Wives, be in subjection to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord. Husbands, love your wives, and don’t be bitter against them.

ends.sectionTitle: Unity and the New Life; the Household; the Armour of God
ends.excerpt: Wives, be subject to your own husbands, as to the Lord. For the husband is the head of the wife, as Christ also is the head of the assembly, being himself the savior of the body.

sources.author: Raymond E. Brown
sources.title: An Introduction to the New Testament
sources.locator: the chapter on Ephesians (its relation to Colossians)

connections.label: The old self and the new
connections.explanation: Ephesians 4:22–24 echoes Colossians 3:9–10: the old self is put off and the new put on, renewed after God's likeness. Colossians speaks of a new self renewed in knowledge after its Creator's image; Ephesians speaks of being renewed in the spirit of the mind and of a new self created in righteousness and holiness.

ends.sectionTitle: The New Life; the Household; Greetings
ends.excerpt: Don’t lie to one another, seeing that you have put off the old man with his doings, and have put on the new man, who is being renewed in knowledge after the image of his Creator,

ends.sectionTitle: Unity and the New Life; the Household; the Armour of God
ends.excerpt: that you put away, as concerning your former way of life, the old man that grows corrupt after the lusts of deceit,

sources.author: Raymond E. Brown
sources.title: An Introduction to the New Testament
sources.locator: the chapter on Ephesians (its relation to Colossians)

connections.label: Psalms, hymns and spiritual songs
connections.explanation: Ephesians 5:19–20 echoes Colossians 3:16–17: believers are to sing psalms, hymns and spiritual songs from the heart and give thanks to God in the name of the Lord Jesus. In Colossians the singing comes from Christ's word dwelling richly among them; in Ephesians it comes from being filled with the Spirit.

ends.sectionTitle: The New Life; the Household; Greetings
ends.excerpt: Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly; in all wisdom teaching and admonishing one another with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your heart to the Lord.

ends.sectionTitle: Unity and the New Life; the Household; the Armour of God
ends.excerpt: speaking to one another in psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs; singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord;

sources.author: Raymond E. Brown
sources.title: An Introduction to the New Testament
sources.locator: the chapter on Ephesians (its relation to Colossians)

connections.label: Tychicus carries the letter
connections.explanation: Ephesians 6:21–22 retells Colossians 4:7–8: both letters close by commending Tychicus, the beloved brother and faithful servant, sent so that the readers may know how Paul is and be comforted. The two passages run almost word for word, one of the longest stretches of shared wording between two New Testament letters.

ends.sectionTitle: The New Life; the Household; Greetings
ends.excerpt: All my affairs will be made known to you by Tychicus, the beloved brother, faithful servant, and fellow bondservant in the Lord.

ends.sectionTitle: Unity and the New Life; the Household; the Armour of God
ends.excerpt: But that you also may know my affairs, how I am doing, Tychicus, the beloved brother and faithful servant in the Lord, will make known to you all things.

sources.author: Raymond E. Brown
sources.title: An Introduction to the New Testament
sources.locator: the chapter on Ephesians (its relation to Colossians)

connections.label: The head of the body, the church
connections.explanation: Ephesians 1:22–23 echoes Colossians 1:18: Christ is the head of the body, which is the church. Colossians adds that he is the beginning and the firstborn from the dead; Ephesians that God has put all things under his feet, and that the church is his fullness.

ends.sectionTitle: The Supremacy of Christ; Warnings against False Teaching
ends.excerpt: He is the head of the body, the assembly, who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, that in all things he might have the preeminence.

ends.sectionTitle: God’s Plan and the One New People
ends.excerpt: He put all things in subjection under his feet, and gave him to be head over all things for the assembly,

sources.author: Raymond E. Brown
sources.title: An Introduction to the New Testament
sources.locator: the chapter on Ephesians (its relation to Colossians)

connections.label: Fallen angels and Sodom
connections.explanation: 2 Peter 2:4–6 retells Jude 1:6–7: the angels who sinned are kept in darkness for the judgement, and Sodom and Gomorrah stand as an example of what comes to the ungodly. Jude speaks of angels who left their proper dwelling and of cities that suffer eternal fire; Second Peter adds Noah, preserved with seven others when the flood came on the ungodly.

ends.excerpt: Angels who didn’t keep their first domain, but deserted their own dwelling place, he has kept in everlasting bonds under darkness for the judgment of the great day.

ends.sectionTitle: Growing in Grace; False Teachers; the Day of the Lord
ends.excerpt: For if God didn’t spare angels when they sinned, but cast them down to Tartarus, and committed them to pits of darkness to be reserved for judgment;

sources.author: Raymond E. Brown
sources.title: An Introduction to the New Testament
sources.locator: the chapter on 2 Peter (its use of Jude)

connections.label: The way of Balaam
connections.explanation: 2 Peter 2:15–16 retells Jude 1:11: the false teachers have gone the way of Balaam, who loved the wages of wrongdoing. Jude sets Balaam beside Cain and Korah; Second Peter tells how a speechless donkey spoke with a man's voice and stopped the prophet's madness.

ends.excerpt: Woe to them! For they went in the way of Cain, and ran riotously in the error of Balaam for hire, and perished in Korah’s rebellion.

ends.sectionTitle: Growing in Grace; False Teachers; the Day of the Lord
ends.excerpt: Forsaking the right way, they went astray, having followed the way of Balaam the son of Beor, who loved the wages of wrongdoing;

sources.author: Raymond E. Brown
sources.title: An Introduction to the New Testament
sources.locator: the chapter on 2 Peter (its use of Jude)

connections.label: Scoffers in the last days
connections.explanation: 2 Peter 3:2–3 retells Jude 1:17–18: readers are to remember what the apostles said beforehand, that scoffers would come in the last days following their own desires. Second Peter adds what the scoffers say, asking where the promise of his coming is.

ends.excerpt: But you, beloved, remember the words which have been spoken before by the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ.

ends.sectionTitle: Growing in Grace; False Teachers; the Day of the Lord
ends.excerpt: that you should remember the words which were spoken before by the holy prophets and the commandment of us, the apostles of the Lord and Savior,

sources.author: Raymond E. Brown
sources.title: An Introduction to the New Testament
sources.locator: the chapter on 2 Peter (its use of Jude)

connections.label: Abraham believed God
connections.explanation: Galatians 3:6–9 and Romans 4:1–3 both tell that Abraham believed God and it was counted to him as righteousness, quoting Genesis to show that righteousness comes through faith. Galatians draws from it that those of faith are Abraham's children and that the nations are blessed in him; Romans asks what Abraham gained and answers that it was not by works.

ends.excerpt: Even so, Abraham “believed God, and it was counted to him for righteousness.” Know therefore that those who are of faith are children of Abraham.

ends.sectionTitle: Abraham’s Faith; Peace with God; Adam and Christ
ends.excerpt: What then will we say that Abraham, our forefather, has found according to the flesh? For if Abraham was justified by works, he has something to boast about, but not toward God.

sources.author: Raymond E. Brown
sources.title: An Introduction to the New Testament
sources.locator: the chapters on Paul's undisputed letters (their order and dates)

connections.label: Abba, Father
connections.explanation: Galatians 4:6–7 and Romans 8:15–17 both tell that the Spirit makes believers God's children, crying Abba, Father, and so heirs. Galatians says they are no longer slaves but sons; Romans adds that they are joint heirs with Christ, suffering with him so as to be glorified with him.

ends.excerpt: And because you are children, God sent out the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, “Abba, Father!”
For you didn’t receive the spirit of bondage again to fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry, “Abba! Father!”

sources.author: Raymond E. Brown
sources.title: An Introduction to the New Testament
sources.locator: the chapters on Paul's undisputed letters (their order and dates)

connections.label: The whole law in one word
connections.explanation: Galatians 5:14 and Romans 13:8–10 both tell that the law is fulfilled in one command, to love your neighbour as yourself. Romans names the commandments against adultery, murder, theft and coveting as summed up in it, and adds that love does no harm to a neighbour.

ends.sectionTitle: Freedom and Life in the Spirit
ends.excerpt: For the whole law is fulfilled in one word, in this: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”

ends.sectionTitle: Life in the Body; Love and the Authorities
ends.excerpt: Owe no one anything, except to love one another; for he who loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law.

sources.author: Raymond E. Brown
sources.title: An Introduction to the New Testament
sources.locator: the chapters on Paul's undisputed letters (their order and dates)

connections.label: Not by works of the law
connections.explanation: Galatians 2:16 and Romans 3:20–28 both tell that a person is put right with God through faith in Jesus Christ and not by doing what the law commands. In Galatians Paul says it to Peter at Antioch; in Romans it closes his argument that all have sinned and are justified freely by God's grace.

ends.excerpt: yet knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ, even we believed in Christ Jesus, that we might be justified by faith in Christ and not by the works…

ends.sectionTitle: The Gospel; All under Sin; Righteousness through Faith
ends.excerpt: Because by the works of the law, no flesh will be justified in his sight; for through the law comes the knowledge of sin.

sources.author: Raymond E. Brown
sources.title: An Introduction to the New Testament
sources.locator: the chapters on Paul's undisputed letters (their order and dates)

connections.label: One body with many members
connections.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:12–27 and Romans 12:4–8 both tell that believers are one body in Christ with many members, each with its own gift. First Corinthians plays out the figure with the foot, the hand, the eye and the ear; Romans lists prophecy, serving, teaching, exhortation, giving, leading and mercy.

ends.sectionTitle: Gifts of the Spirit and the Way of Love
ends.excerpt: For as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the body, being many, are one body; so also is Christ.

ends.sectionTitle: Life in the Body; Love and the Authorities
ends.excerpt: For even as we have many members in one body, and all the members don’t have the same function,

sources.author: Raymond E. Brown
sources.title: An Introduction to the New Testament
sources.locator: the chapters on Paul's undisputed letters (their order and dates)

connections.label: Adam and Christ
connections.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:20–22 and Romans 5:12–19 both tell of Adam and Christ as the two men through whom death and life came. First Corinthians says that as all die in Adam, all will be made alive in Christ; Romans sets one man's trespass against one man's obedience and the gift of grace.

ends.excerpt: But now Christ has been raised from the dead. He became the first fruit of those who are asleep.

ends.sectionTitle: Abraham’s Faith; Peace with God; Adam and Christ
ends.excerpt: Therefore, as sin entered into the world through one man, and death through sin, so death passed to all men because all sinned.

sources.author: Raymond E. Brown
sources.title: An Introduction to the New Testament
sources.locator: the chapters on Paul's undisputed letters (their order and dates)

connections.label: The trumpet and the raising of the dead
connections.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 4:15–17 and 1 Corinthians 15:51–52 both tell that at the sound of the trumpet the dead will be raised and those still living will not be left behind. First Thessalonians says the living will be caught up with them in the clouds to meet the Lord; First Corinthians that all will be changed in the twinkling of an eye.

ends.excerpt: For this we tell you by the word of the Lord, that we who are alive, who are left until the coming of the Lord, will in no way precede those who have fallen asleep.
Behold, I tell you a mystery. We will not all sleep, but we will all be changed, in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound and the dead will be raised…

sources.author: Raymond E. Brown
sources.title: An Introduction to the New Testament
sources.locator: the chapters on Paul's undisputed letters (their order and dates)

connections.label: The armour of God
connections.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:8 and Ephesians 6:13–17 both tell of the believer armed for the fight, with a breastplate and the hope of salvation for a helmet. First Thessalonians names the breastplate faith and love; Ephesians gives the whole armour, with truth as a belt, righteousness as a breastplate, faith as a shield and the word of God as the Spirit's sword.

ends.excerpt: But since we belong to the day, let’s be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and love, and for a helmet, the hope of salvation.

ends.sectionTitle: Unity and the New Life; the Household; the Armour of God
ends.excerpt: Therefore put on the whole armor of God, that you may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand.

sources.author: Raymond E. Brown
sources.title: An Introduction to the New Testament
sources.locator: the chapters on Paul's undisputed letters (their order and dates)

connections.label: A new creation
connections.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:17 and Galatians 6:15 both tell that in Christ there is a new creation. Second Corinthians adds that the old things have passed away; Galatians says that neither circumcision nor uncircumcision counts for anything, but only the new creation.

ends.sectionTitle: Ministers of the New Covenant; Reconciliation
ends.excerpt: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.

ends.sectionTitle: Freedom and Life in the Spirit
ends.excerpt: For in Christ Jesus neither is circumcision anything, nor uncircumcision, but a new creation.

connections.label: A Hebrew of Hebrews
connections.explanation: 2 Corinthians 11:22 and Philippians 3:4–6 both tell Paul's own descent when others boast of theirs: a Hebrew, an Israelite, of Abraham's line. Philippians adds his circumcision on the eighth day, his tribe of Benjamin, his life as a Pharisee and a persecutor, and then counts all of it as loss for Christ.

ends.excerpt: Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they the offspring of Abraham? So am I.
though I myself might have confidence even in the flesh. If any other man thinks that he has confidence in the flesh, I yet more:

connections.label: The words over the bread and cup
connections.explanation: 1 Corinthians 11:23–25 and Matthew 26:26–28 both tell the words of Jesus at the supper: the bread his body, the cup the covenant in his blood. Paul hands it on as received from the Lord, with the command to do this in memory of him; Matthew has the blood poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.

ends.sectionTitle: Order in Worship; the Lord’s Supper
ends.excerpt: For I received from the Lord that which also I delivered to you, that the Lord Jesus on the night in which he was betrayed took bread.

ends.sectionTitle: The Last Supper and the Arrest
ends.excerpt: As they were eating, Jesus took bread, gave thanks for it, and broke it. He gave to the disciples and said, “Take, eat; this is my body.”

sources.author: Raymond E. Brown
sources.title: An Introduction to the New Testament
sources.locator: the chapters on Paul's undisputed letters and on Matthew and Mark (dates of writing)

connections.label: Not I, but the Lord
connections.explanation: 1 Corinthians 7:10–11 and Mark 10:9–12 both tell the Lord's command against divorce. Paul marks it as the Lord's word rather than his own, that a wife should not leave her husband nor a husband his wife; Mark gives Jesus' saying that what God has joined no one should separate, and his answer to the disciples in the house.

ends.excerpt: But to the married I command—not I, but the Lord—that the wife not leave her husband (but if she departs, let her remain unmarried, or else be reconciled to her husband), and that the husband not…
What therefore God has joined together, let no man separate.” In the house, his disciples asked him again about the same matter.

sources.author: Raymond E. Brown
sources.title: An Introduction to the New Testament
sources.locator: the chapters on Paul's undisputed letters and on Matthew and Mark (dates of writing)

connections.label: Like a thief in the night
connections.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:2 and Matthew 24:42–44 both tell that the Lord's coming will be like a thief's, at an hour no one expects. Paul reminds the Thessalonians that they already know the Lord's day will come as a thief does, by night; Matthew gives the saying about the householder who would have watched had he known the hour.

ends.excerpt: For you yourselves know well that the day of the Lord comes like a thief in the night. For when they are saying, “Peace and safety,” then sudden destruction will come on them, like birth pains on a…
Watch therefore, for you don’t know in what hour your Lord comes. But know this, that if the master of the house had known in what watch of the night the thief was coming, he would have watched, and…

sources.author: Raymond E. Brown
sources.title: An Introduction to the New Testament
sources.locator: the chapters on 1 Thessalonians and on Matthew (dates of writing)

connections.label: I will come as a thief
connections.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:2 and Revelation 3:3 both tell that the Lord will come like a thief to those who are not awake. Paul tells the Thessalonians the Lord's day will come as a thief comes, by night; in Revelation the risen Christ warns the church in Sardis that if it does not watch, he will come as a thief at an hour it will not know.

ends.excerpt: For you yourselves know well that the day of the Lord comes like a thief in the night. For when they are saying, “Peace and safety,” then sudden destruction will come on them, like birth pains on a…
Remember therefore how you have received and heard. Keep it and repent. If therefore you won’t watch, I will come as a thief, and you won’t know what hour I will come upon you.

sources.author: Raymond E. Brown
sources.title: An Introduction to the New Testament
sources.locator: the chapters on 1 Thessalonians and on Revelation (dates of writing)

connections.label: Abraham justified by faith, or by works
connections.explanation: Romans 4:1–3 is set against James 2:21–24: both cite the word that Abraham believed God and it was counted to him as righteousness. Romans says Abraham was not justified by works, or he would have something to boast of; James says he was justified by works when he offered Isaac, faith working with his deeds. Readers since have weighed how the two fit together.

ends.sectionTitle: Abraham’s Faith; Peace with God; Adam and Christ
ends.excerpt: What then will we say that Abraham, our forefather, has found according to the flesh? For if Abraham was justified by works, he has something to boast about, but not toward God.

ends.sectionTitle: Trials; Hearing and Doing; Faith and Works
ends.excerpt: Wasn’t Abraham our father justified by works, in that he offered up Isaac his son on the altar?

connections.label: God resists the proud
connections.explanation: James 4:6–10 and 1 Peter 5:5–9 both tell that God resists the proud but gives grace to the humble, and call readers to humble themselves before God and resist the devil. James promises that the devil will flee and that God will lift up the humble; First Peter pictures the devil as a roaring lion looking for someone to devour.

ends.sectionTitle: The Tongue, Humility, the Rich, Patience and Prayer
ends.excerpt: But he gives more grace. Therefore it says, “God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”

ends.sectionTitle: Suffering for Doing Good; Shepherds of the Flock
ends.excerpt: Likewise, you younger ones, be subject to the elder. Yes, all of you clothe yourselves with humility and subject yourselves to one another; for “God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”

connections.label: The image of God, through whom all was made
connections.explanation: Colossians 1:15–17 and Hebrews 1:2–3 both tell of the Son as the image of God through whom all things were made and in whom they hold together. Colossians calls him the image of the invisible God and the firstborn of all creation; Hebrews calls him the radiance of God's glory and the very image of his substance, upholding all things by his word.

ends.sectionTitle: The Supremacy of Christ; Warnings against False Teaching
ends.excerpt: He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation. For by him all things were created in the heavens and on the earth, visible things and invisible things, whether thrones or…

ends.sectionTitle: The Son above the Angels and Moses; the Promised Rest
ends.excerpt: has at the end of these days spoken to us by his Son, whom he appointed heir of all things, through whom also he made the worlds.

connections.label: Coming with the clouds
connections.explanation: Matthew 24:30 and Revelation 1:7 both tell of the Son of Man coming with the clouds and all the tribes of the earth mourning when they see him. Matthew gives it as Jesus' word on the Mount of Olives; Revelation opens with it, adding that those who pierced him will see him.

ends.excerpt: and then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in the sky. Then all the tribes of the earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of the sky with power and great glory.
Behold, he is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see him, including those who pierced him. All the tribes of the earth will mourn over him. Even so, Amen.

connections.label: Let your yes be yes
connections.explanation: Matthew 5:34–37 and James 5:12 both tell the command not to swear at all, neither by heaven nor by earth, but to let a yes be yes and a no be no. Matthew gives it in the Sermon on the Mount; James repeats it above all things, so that his readers do not fall under judgement.

ends.sectionTitle: The Sermon on the Mount: the Beatitudes and the Law
ends.excerpt: but I tell you, don’t swear at all: neither by heaven, for it is the throne of God; nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of his feet; nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.

ends.sectionTitle: The Tongue, Humility, the Rich, Patience and Prayer
ends.excerpt: But above all things, my brothers, don’t swear—not by heaven, or by the earth, or by any other oath; but let your “yes” be “yes”, and your “no”, “no”, so that you don’t fall into hypocrisy.

connections.label: Blessed when you suffer for righteousness
connections.explanation: Matthew 5:10–12 and 1 Peter 3:14 both tell that those who suffer for righteousness' sake are blessed. Matthew gives it among the Beatitudes, with the promise of the Kingdom; First Peter applies it to believers slandered for doing good, and tells them not to fear what others fear.

ends.sectionTitle: The Sermon on the Mount: the Beatitudes and the Law
ends.excerpt: Blessed are those who have been persecuted for righteousness’ sake, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.

ends.sectionTitle: Suffering for Doing Good; Shepherds of the Flock
ends.excerpt: But even if you should suffer for righteousness’ sake, you are blessed. “Don’t fear what they fear, neither be troubled.”

connections.label: Subject to the governing authorities
connections.explanation: Romans 13:1–7 and 1 Peter 2:13–17 both tell believers to submit to the governing authorities, who punish wrongdoers and praise those who do good. Romans says every authority is from God and that taxes and honour are owed to whom they are due; First Peter tells readers to honour all people, love the brothers, fear God and honour the king.

ends.sectionTitle: Life in the Body; Love and the Authorities
ends.excerpt: Let every soul be in subjection to the higher authorities, for there is no authority except from God, and those who exist are ordained by God.

ends.sectionTitle: New Birth and Hope; a Holy People
ends.excerpt: Therefore subject yourselves to every ordinance of man for the Lord’s sake: whether to the king, as supreme,

connections.label: Our beloved brother Paul
connections.explanation: 2 Peter 3:15–16 names Romans 2:4: Second Peter tells readers to count the Lord's patience as salvation, as Paul wrote in all his letters. Romans speaks in those terms, asking whether the reader despises God's kindness and patience, which lead to repentance. Second Peter adds that some things in Paul's letters are hard to understand, and are twisted by the unstable.

ends.sectionTitle: The Gospel; All under Sin; Righteousness through Faith
ends.excerpt: Or do you despise the riches of his goodness, forbearance, and patience, not knowing that the goodness of God leads you to repentance?

ends.sectionTitle: Growing in Grace; False Teachers; the Day of the Lord
ends.excerpt: Regard the patience of our Lord as salvation; even as our beloved brother Paul also, according to the wisdom given to him, wrote to you,

connections.label: The same names in two letters
connections.explanation: Colossians 4:10–14 and Philemon 1:23–24 both tell of the same companions sending greetings with Paul: Epaphras, Mark, Aristarchus, Demas and Luke. Colossians adds that Epaphras wrestles in prayer for them and that Luke is the beloved physician. The shared names tie the two letters to one time and place.

ends.sectionTitle: The New Life; the Household; Greetings
ends.excerpt: Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner, greets you, and Mark the cousin of Barnabas (concerning whom you received instructions, “if he comes to you, receive him”),
Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, greets you, as do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, my fellow workers.

connections.label: Onesimus sent back
connections.explanation: Colossians 4:9 and Philemon 1:10–12 both tell of Onesimus going back to Colossae. Colossians sends him with Tychicus as a faithful and beloved brother who is one of them; Philemon tells his story, a once useless servant who became Paul's child in prison and is now useful, sent back to be received as Paul himself.

ends.sectionTitle: The New Life; the Household; Greetings
ends.excerpt: together with Onesimus, the faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you. They will make known to you everything that is going on here.
I appeal to you for my child Onesimus, whom I have become the father of in my chains, who once was useless to you, but now is useful to you and to me.

connections.label: Jesus Christ come in the flesh
connections.explanation: 1 John 4:2–3 and 2 John 1:7 both tell that whoever does not confess Jesus Christ come in the flesh is not of God, and name that spirit the antichrist. First John gives it as the test of every spirit; Second John warns of many deceivers gone out into the world.

ends.sectionTitle: Children of God; Love and Faith
ends.excerpt: By this you know the Spirit of God: every spirit who confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is of God,

ends.sectionTitle: A Letter to a Church: Truth and Love
ends.excerpt: For many deceivers have gone out into the world, those who don’t confess that Jesus Christ came in the flesh. This is the deceiver and the Antichrist.

connections.label: Not a new commandment
connections.explanation: 1 John 2:7–8 and 2 John 1:5–6 both tell that the commandment they write is no new one but the one held from the beginning. First John adds that it is new too, since the darkness is passing; Second John says plainly that the commandment is to love one another, and that love is walking in his commandments.

ends.excerpt: Brothers, I write no new commandment to you, but an old commandment which you had from the beginning. The old commandment is the word which you heard from the beginning.

ends.sectionTitle: A Letter to a Church: Truth and Love
ends.excerpt: Now I beg you, dear lady, not as though I wrote to you a new commandment, but that which we had from the beginning, that we love one another.

connections.label: Whoever does good is of God
connections.explanation: 1 John 3:10 and 3 John 1:11 both tell that what a person does shows whether he is of God. First John says whoever does not do righteousness or love his brother is not of God; Third John urges Gaius to imitate the good, since whoever does good is of God and whoever does evil has not seen him.

ends.sectionTitle: Children of God; Love and Faith
ends.excerpt: In this the children of God are revealed, and the children of the devil. Whoever doesn’t do righteousness is not of God, neither is he who doesn’t love his brother.
Beloved, don’t imitate that which is evil, but that which is good. He who does good is of God. He who does evil hasn’t seen God.

connections.label: What an overseer must be
connections.explanation: 1 Timothy 3:1–7 and Titus 1:5–9 both tell what is asked of an overseer: blameless, the husband of one wife, hospitable, not given to wine, violence or greed, ruling his household well. First Timothy adds that he must not be a new convert; Titus that he must hold to sound teaching, as elders are appointed in every city of Crete.

ends.sectionTitle: Sound Teaching; Prayer; Overseers and Deacons
ends.excerpt: This is a faithful saying: someone who seeks to be an overseer desires a good work. The overseer therefore must be without reproach, the husband of one wife, temperate, sensible, modest, hospitable…
I left you in Crete for this reason, that you would set in order the things that were lacking and appoint elders in every city, as I directed you—

connections.label: The teaching of Balaam
connections.explanation: Jude 1:11 and Revelation 2:14 both tell of Balaam as the pattern of those who lead God's people astray. Jude sets him beside Cain and Korah as one who erred for reward; in Revelation the risen Christ warns Pergamum about those who hold the teaching of Balaam, who taught Balak to entice Israel to idol feasts and sexual immorality.

ends.excerpt: Woe to them! For they went in the way of Cain, and ran riotously in the error of Balaam for hire, and perished in Korah’s rebellion.
But I have a few things against you, because you have there some who hold the teaching of Balaam, who taught Balak to throw a stumbling block before the children of Israel, to eat things sacrificed…

connections.label: A new heaven and a new earth
connections.explanation: 2 Peter 3:13 and Revelation 21:1 both tell of the new heavens and new earth that believers wait for. Second Peter says righteousness dwells there after the present heavens are dissolved; Revelation sees them, the first heaven and earth passed away and the sea no more.

ends.sectionTitle: Growing in Grace; False Teachers; the Day of the Lord
ends.excerpt: But, according to his promise, we look for new heavens and a new earth, in which righteousness dwells.
I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth have passed away, and the sea is no more.

connections.label: Milk, not solid food
connections.explanation: 1 Corinthians 3:1–2 and Hebrews 5:12–14 both tell of believers who still need milk, not solid food. Paul says he could not speak to the Corinthians as spiritual but as infants in Christ; Hebrews says its readers ought to be teachers by now, and that solid food is for the mature, trained to tell good from evil.

ends.sectionTitle: Divisions and the Wisdom of the Cross
ends.excerpt: Brothers, I couldn’t speak to you as to spiritual, but as to fleshly, as to babies in Christ.
For although by this time you should be teachers, you again need to have someone teach you the rudiments of the first principles of the revelations of God. You have come to need milk, and not solid…

connections.label: The voice on the holy mountain
connections.explanation: Matthew 17:1–5 and 2 Peter 1:16–18 both tell of the voice that named Jesus the beloved Son on the mountain. Matthew tells the Transfiguration itself; Second Peter appeals to it as eyewitness testimony, saying that the writer heard the voice from heaven while with him on the holy mountain.

ends.excerpt: After six days, Jesus took with him Peter, James, and John his brother, and brought them up into a high mountain by themselves.

ends.sectionTitle: Growing in Grace; False Teachers; the Day of the Lord
ends.excerpt: For we didn’t follow cunningly devised fables when we made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but we were eyewitnesses of his majesty.

connections.label: Work with your own hands
connections.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 4:11–12 and 2 Thessalonians 3:10–12 both tell the Thessalonians to live quietly and earn their own bread. The first letter asks them to mind their own business and work with their hands; the second recalls the rule that whoever will not work should not eat, and rebukes those who have turned busybodies.

ends.excerpt: and that you make it your ambition to lead a quiet life, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands, even as we instructed you,

ends.sectionTitle: Endurance; the Day of the Lord; Idleness
ends.excerpt: For even when we were with you, we commanded you this: “If anyone is not willing to work, don’t let him eat.”
